headline: High: shared filesystem and broad egress make prompt injection, leakage, and cascading errors plausible by default in the AutoGPT–Flowise pair.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: AutoGPT can read and act on filesystem content, while Flowise writes uploaded files and server filesystem artifacts; that shared file channel can carry attacker-controlled text into AutoGPT’s instruction stream. No MCP/clipboard bridge is shown, so this is not high, but the pathway exists in common deployments.
conditions: IF Flowise writes a file that AutoGPT later ingests as task context or instructions
IF both agents share the same workspace directory without content provenance checks
mitigations: Separate workspaces per agent
Disable automatic ingestion of uploaded files into AutoGPT prompts
Add provenance tags to files before AutoGPT reads them
Review shared directories for prompt-like content before handoff
requires-engineering: enforce file-level trust boundaries

B_data_leakage.rationale: Flowise touches chatflow inputs/outputs and stores uploaded files on the server filesystem, while AutoGPT can read files and make allowlisted network calls. If sensitive data enters Flowise, AutoGPT can re-read it and potentially transmit it through its egress path; the pair therefore has a default leakage pathway.
conditions: IF sensitive chatflow inputs or uploaded files are stored in Flowise’s server filesystem
IF AutoGPT is configured to read those files and call external APIs with their contents
mitigations: Store sensitive files outside the shared workspace
Restrict AutoGPT to non-sensitive directories
Turn off or narrow AutoGPT network egress
Redact secrets before Flowise persists inputs
requires-engineering: add DLP scanning on file handoff

C_capability_conflict.rationale: AutoGPT can execute shell commands and spawn subprocesses, while Flowise can write the server filesystem and supports multiple instances with shared state via server datastore. That creates overlapping mutation of shared resources without any locking evidence, so concurrent corruption or overwrite is a realistic default risk.
conditions: IF both agents target the same directory or datastore
IF Flowise instances run concurrently while AutoGPT writes files or subprocess outputs into the same path
mitigations: Assign disjoint write paths
Serialize writes with a lock file
Run only one Flowise instance per shared workspace
Make AutoGPT write to a temp directory
requires-engineering: add transactional coordination for shared state

D_cascading_error.rationale: Flowise is a graph-based orchestrator that can route tool outputs, and AutoGPT can generate intermediate facts or files that Flowise may treat as inputs. Without a documented verification step between them, erroneous AutoGPT output can cascade into downstream tool actions or user-visible results.
conditions: IF Flowise consumes AutoGPT-produced text or files as authoritative node input
IF downstream Flowise nodes act on that content without validation
mitigations: Insert a human review step before action nodes
Require schema validation on AutoGPT outputs
Mark AutoGPT outputs as untrusted in Flowise
Limit downstream nodes to read-only operations
requires-engineering: add verifier nodes between agents

E_compliance.rationale: Flowise explicitly handles chatflow inputs/outputs and model provider/tool credentials, while AutoGPT can egress data to external APIs. Even without a stated residency mismatch, the pair can move regulated content into third-party services and logs unless operators configure retention and redaction carefully.
conditions: IF regulated data is placed into Flowise chatflows or uploaded files
IF either agent forwards that data to external model providers or tools
mitigations: Avoid regulated data in shared flows
Disable logging of sensitive prompts and files
Rotate and scope tool credentials narrowly
Set short retention on chatflow artifacts
requires-engineering: implement residency-aware routing
